newsitem.title: JAPAN: June JGBs end higher on hectic cash bond buying.
newsitem.headline: June JGBs end higher on hectic cash bond buying.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended just off its day's high on Thursday, due to hectic cash bond buying from banks and brokers.
"Recent persistent buying from institutional investors fuelled fears that we might miss a chance to buy," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.

Buying from some life insurers was detected in long-term JGBs and this encouraged all kinds of dealers to follow suit, traders said. The June contract rose for the fourth straight day, ending at 126.25, up 0.50 from Wednesday's close.

The yield of key 182nd 10-year JGBs hit another record low of 2.240 percent in the afternoon. It stood even with the record low at 0645 GMT, down 0.060 from Wednesday. The yield has been renewing the record lows every day since Tuesday.
The key June futures contract moved between 125.77 and 126.26 with a huge 78,764 contracts changing hands.
Buyers of the key June contract were said to have included foreign hedge funds who had gone short earlier.
A rumour, later denied, that Daiwa Securities would hold a news conference on client accounts linked with racketeers, also provided support, traders said.
A Daiwa spokesman said it was currently undergoing a routine inspection by Japan's securities watchdog, which began on March 3, but it was not related to suspicious deals.

Investors are eager to accumulate cash JGBs from the start of the new fiscal year in April and some of them were starting in advance, traders said. That was based on a widespread view that Japanese interest rates will not be raised in the April-June period.
Buying from some life insurers this week was attributed to window-dressing for their book closings, they said. JGBs to be traded on and after March 21 are settled in the new year.

"Those who had expected to buy on dips and those who had sold when the key 182nd JGB yield fell below three percent were in a hurry to increase their JGB holdings ahead of the fiscal year-end," said a senior fund manger at a Japanese life insurance.
The market was also supported by expectations that there will be no bearish factors in sight, he said.

The Bank of Japan's tankan quartery survey due on April 2 is unlikely to show a bright picture for the economic recovery. Also, the demand-supply condition in the April-June period is expected to be more favourable than a year ago, he said.

Traders said the JGB market may stay supported by extra cash emerging in June from maturing JGBs of over four trillion yen and the Housing Loan Administrative Corp's decision to make a loan repayment of 1.2 trillion yen to agricultural financial bodies at the end of March. The amount of privately placed municipal bonds issued between March and May could be about one trillion yen smaller than usual, they added.
Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) data released at 0630 GMT had little impact on JGBs as a real 1.0 percent rise in the October-December period was within expectations, traders said.
